newsitem.title: USA: US 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates dip in wk-Freddie Mac.
newsitem.headline: US 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates dip in wk-Freddie Mac.

text.p: The average commitment rate on U.S. 30-year fixed rate mortgages dipped to 8.08 percent in the week ending April 25 from 8.16 percent the prior week, while 15-year mortgages fell to 7.62 percent from 7.71 percent, Freddie Mac said Thursday.
One-year adjustable rate mortgages also inched downward to an average 5.86 percent from 5.89 percent, it said.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 7.92 percent, the 15-year 7.43 percent and the ARM 5.74 percent.

"The economy is still strong, but we have not seen signs of inflation in the Consumer Price Index, which has been running fairly consistent at about three percent," Robert Van Order, Freddie Mac chief economist, said.
"Monday we should get news about the volume of new home sales and this will have some impact on mortgage interest rates next week and in the near future," Van Order added.
The Labor Department has said U.S. 1996 consumer prices rose at a 3.3 percent seasonally adjusted annual rate, and that March consumer prices rose 0.1 percent.
Next week the Commerce Department will issue U.S. March single-family home sales.
Lenders charged an average 1.7 percent in fees and points on both 30- and 15-year loans, unchanged from last week. They charged 1.5 percent on ARM loans, up from 1.4 percent last week.
Freddie Mac is a corporation chartered by Congress that buys mortgages from lenders and packages them into securities for investors.
